bank: EYES AND EARS -- WHAT MAKES A WALK OR AN IDLE READ WRONG
note: DRAFT MATERIAL, NEVER WIRED INTO THE GAME. REUSE CHECK: three gates already watch animation -- anim_fabrication (a moving limb cannot gain painted pixels), frozen_poses (a hold is the same frame, not a recomputation), motion_visible (the clip moves enough pixels to see). Nothing here re-measures those.

tells.what_it_looks_like: the last frame is not the first frame, so the character snaps back once per loop, forever
tells.how_a_machine_finds_it: the joint vector at phase 0 against the vector one frame before phase 1, in every direction, compared against that clip's own typical step
tells.found: 7 of 102 clips do not close, and ALL SEVEN are one-shot actions. Every clip that is a cycle closes cleanly

tells.what_it_looks_like: one frame where a joint jumps while everything else moves smoothly
tells.how_a_machine_finds_it: the biggest single step against the clip's own median step, so a fast clip is not punished for being fast
tells.found: 16 clips over 6x; the worst are cover-drop 47.8x and cover-rise 34.4x. Some are meant to snap (get-shoved), which is why this is a report and not a verdict

tells.what_it_looks_like: a cycle whose length is not a whole number of beats, so it drifts against the song
tells.how_a_machine_finds_it: the clip's declared beat count; at 120 BPM a beat is 500ms, so 2 and 4 are on the grid and anything else is not
tells.found: 0 of 105 clips are off a 2 or 4 beat count. The 120 BPM law holds across the whole library

tells.what_it_looks_like: a one-shot action played on a loop, popping every cycle
tells.how_a_machine_finds_it: there is no loop flag in the clip table to find. The bench drives every clip with phase modulo 1, one-shots included

tells.what_it_looks_like: the planted foot skates over the ground instead of sticking to it
tells.how_a_machine_finds_it: NOT YET. It needs the foot's position on the ground per frame AND the speed the world moves him at, and the second number lives in the city, not in the pose. Named here so nobody thinks the list is finished

tells.what_it_looks_like: joints appearing and disappearing between frames, which is the morphing family
tells.how_a_machine_finds_it: the set of joint keys returned at each phase; if it changes, the frames are not the same puppet
tells.found: floor-rise changes shape between frames in all eight directions

tells.what_it_looks_like: a name in the clip list with no pose behind it
tells.how_a_machine_finds_it: a name in CLIPS with no entry in POSE
tells.found: sleep and headshot-2. NOT A FAULT: both are driven by a physics simulation and a lying special case instead of the pose table. It is a limit of this instrument and it is written down as one

tells.what_it_looks_like: a walk with only contact poses, so the legs teleport between steps
tells.how_a_machine_finds_it: the number of distinct poses per cycle, which the frozen-poses gate already resolves per clip

tells.what_it_looks_like: a walk with no vertical bob, so the body floats
tells.how_a_machine_finds_it: the vertical component of the hip offset across a cycle; it should have two dips per stride

tells.tell: the arms do not oppose the legs
tells.what_it_looks_like: same-side arm and leg swinging together, which reads as a toy
tells.how_a_machine_finds_it: the sign correlation between arm and thigh over a cycle; the contralateral law is already written into the walk pose, so this is a regression test rather than a discovery
